canonical.title: Minimum bit flips
canonical.sourceFilePath: 06.Bit Manipulation/2. Interview Problems/01. Minimum bit flips.cpp

narrative.title: Re-Programming the Robot's Mode Register
narrative.scenario: A warehouse robot's mode register must change from its current setting to a goal setting, and each reprogramming run flips exactly one bit. The maintenance log wants the minimum number of flip runs. XOR-ing the two registers leaves a 1 in every position that disagrees, so the answer is simply how many 1s survive that comparison.
narrative.outputFormat: The minimum number of bit flips to turn start into goal.

complexity.optimalTime: O(log n) — one pass over the differing bits (fixed 32 in the source)

testCases.explanation: 1010 vs 0111 differ in three positions, so three flips are both necessary and sufficient.
011 vs 100 disagree everywhere — every bit must be flipped.

hintLevels: Level 1: A flip only matters where the two registers disagree — find those positions first.
Level 2: start ^ goal lights exactly the mismatched bits; the answer is its popcount.
Level 3: Repeatedly clear the lowest set bit (x &= x - 1) to count without scanning all 32 slots.
